name: Griffith College Dublin
feeMethod: A private college that charges one flat non-EU tuition for all undergraduate degrees and one standard rate for most master's, plus fixed yearly college fees; the calculator uses those flat rates.
description: Griffith College is Ireland's largest private higher education college, founded in 1974 with its main campus on South Circular Road in Dublin and further campuses in Cork and Limerick. It is not a university: its degrees are validated by QQI (Quality and Qualifications Ireland), the state agency for qualifications.
whyIncluded: One of the 10 universities in Ireland most popular with international students; Ireland is one of the nine places Singaporeans most often study abroad (about 270 Singaporean students, UNESCO data).

livingCosts.summary: Griffith College's July 2026 cost-of-living guide for international students in Dublin: a single room in a shared apartment, groceries, a monthly Leap card, social activities and books, over a 9-month academic year.
livingCosts.notes: Rung A. Griffith College 'Cost of Living for International Students at Griffith College: What to Expect' PDF (v3.1, published July 2026), which budgets over a 9-month academic year. Midpoints of the guide's monthly ranges: housing = 'Single room in a shared apartment: EUR 600-1,000+ per month' -> 800 (shared house 500-900+, studio 1,200+); food = 'Monthly food/grocery costs: 250-400' -> 325; transport = 'Monthly transport costs: 50-60' -> 55 (Leap card registration 5 excluded); personal = social activities 80-150 -> 115 plus stationery and books 100-150 -> 125 = 240. The PDF's summary table is mis-set (every 'average monthly' cell shows 600) so the prose ranges were used; its 'Maximum Cost (9 months)' total is 15,300 (1,700/month) and average yearly total 12,960, consistent with this 1,420/month estimate. Utilities are not mentioned separately. Tuition, flights, visa/IRP excluded.

programmes.name: BSc (Hons) in Computing Science
programmes.feeBasis: Griffith's single non-EU tuition of €13,500 a year for all undergraduate programmes (Sept 2025 intake onwards), plus €825 of compulsory yearly college fees.
programmes.summary: Yearly tuition for international (non-EU) students plus EUR 825 of compulsory yearly college fees. Griffith reviews its fees every year.
programmes.notes: Griffith College 'Non-EU Tuition Fees, Scholarships, and Bursaries' undergraduate pack (Nov 2025, linked from griffith.ie/admissions/fees/non-eu-tuition-fees), 'For September 2025 intake onwards': annual tuition EUR 13,500 for all undergraduate programmes. Compulsory 'A.I.P Fees' each academic year: Academic Administration Fee EUR 250 + International Student Support Fee EUR 300 + Protection of Enrolled Learner Fee EUR 275 (once per stage) = EUR 825. A QQI award fee (EUR 200 for Level 8) is charged in the final year only and is not included. Griffith bursaries by faculty (e.g. EUR 500 for Computing Science at GC Dublin) and merit scholarships may reduce tuition; not applied. The same pack is the live fee document for September 2026 entry, so the 2026 fee and the 2025 history row are the same published figure. Degree validated by QQI. 4 years full-time, Dublin and Cork. 2024 row: Griffith's non-EU undergraduate pack 'Updated February 2024' (the schedule in force before the September 2025 change): 'EUR 12,000 For all undergraduate programmes (No increase since December 2022)', with Academic Administration Fee EUR 250 + International Student Support Fee EUR 200 + Protection of Enrolled Learner Fee EUR 245 = EUR 695.
